expedition.name: Initialize Audit and Evidence Gathering
expedition.goal: Audit the codebase, identify architectural gaps, evaluate usability, and propose follow-up expeditions based on findings.

expedition.name: Fix CLI Next-Command ID Resolution
expedition.goal: Fix the bug where next command suggestions reference incorrect Mission/Expedition IDs when creating or managing drafts to improve robustness and ease of use.

expedition.name: Simplify Expedition Lifecycle Operations
expedition.goal: Consolidate CLI commands to reduce operator toil (e.g. smoother transitions from Draft to Executing, auto-ignoring untracked scratch files) to improve simplification and coherence.

expedition.name: Optimize CLI Bootstrap Performance
expedition.goal: Profile and optimize the 13-step infrastructure bootstrap and event replay to reduce CLI command latency.

expedition.name: Dead Code Elimination (Exports)
expedition.goal: Remove unused exported functions and types across the framework to reduce the API surface and overall codebase size.

expedition.name: Dead Code Elimination (Files)
expedition.goal: Delete orphaned files and modules that are no longer referenced in the dependency graph to reduce bloat.

expedition.name: Dependency Graph Hardening
expedition.goal: Refactor and simplify the internal dependency graph to prevent circular dependencies and improve maintainability.

expedition.name: Address Monolithic State Files in .synth/data/
expedition.goal: Analyze and implement a strategy (such as event log rotation, compaction, or state partitioning) to prevent state files from growing indefinitely and creating performance bottlenecks.

expedition.name: Validation Assertion Quiet Output Flag
expedition.goal: Add a flag/option to the validation engine and CLI to suppress passing test details and only output errors or failing tests, reducing console output saturation.

expedition.name: Remove Legacy Support for Previous Synth Projects
expedition.goal: Deprecate and remove backwards-compatibility layers and migrations designed for legacy Synth v1 projects, simplifying codebase maintenance since there are no active legacy installations in the wild.

expedition.name: Investigate 13 Event System Bureaucracy
expedition.goal: Investigate and propose strategies to alleviate the bureaucracy of the 13-event system in Synth development

expedition.name: Human-Readable Expedition Branch Naming
expedition.goal: Replace cryptic raw-ID branch names with slug-based names (expedition/<mission-slug>/<expedition-slug>-<expId[0:7]>) while preserving determinism, uniqueness, and traceability so checkpoint and branch-policy enforcement still resolve correctly.

expedition.name: Single-Source Branch Naming
expedition.goal: Move branch-name composition out of branch-creation methods into mission/expedition composition; resolve names through a single source of truth; remove redundant legacy/candidate helpers if unneeded; align checkpoint types.

expedition.name: Resolve ExecutionGate legacy-only branch enforcement conflict
expedition.goal: Document and resolve the pre-existing test failure where the ExecutionGate enforces only the legacy branch form while the CLI auto-creates the slug form, causing tests/execution-branch-gate.test.js testCliAutoCreatesCanonicalBranchOnMainUnderEnforce to fail on a fresh dist rebuild

expedition.name: Resolve ExecutionGate legacy-only branch enforcement conflict
expedition.goal: Document and resolve the pre-existing test failure where the ExecutionGate enforces only the legacy branch form while the CLI auto-creates the slug form, causing tests/execution-branch-gate.test.js testCliAutoCreatesCanonicalBranchOnMainUnderEnforce to fail on a fresh dist rebuild

expedition.name: Development Platform Audit: CLI Discoverability, Agent Friendliness, Continuity
expedition.goal: Evidence-gathering / investigation expedition. Sincere audit of SYNTH as an internal development platform: audit CLI discoverability, agent friendliness, and development continuity; assess what measures are needed to mature into a first-world development platform. Explicitly NOT a feature/tool-producing expedition — output is findings, evidence, and recommendations discussed with the operator.

expedition.name: DRY Self-Review Report Format for Expedition Changes
expedition.goal: Codify the DRY self-review report format and checklist used during Single-Source Branch Naming (expedition 190a72e71fbe3c14) so every expedition verifies its own changes for DRY compliance before PR: (1) enumerate every file changed by the expedition, (2) audit each change for duplication/dead code/redundant helpers, (3) confirm all call sites funnel through a single source of truth, (4) verify removal of parallel implementations, (5) run tsc + affected tests, (6) produce the per-file DRY report table as evidence. Evidence-gathering / process expedition — output is a documented review format, not new framework features.

expedition.name: Fix --dry-run persisting state mutations
expedition.goal: Investigate and fix the --dry-run flag in mutating CLI subcommands (expedition create, delete) so it never persists draft files, canonical-state, or event-log entries. Reproducer: two consecutive dry-run and real expedition-create invocations both logged EXPEDITION_CREATED events and persisted draft files (fdc1558fa0a676d7 was an accidental dry-run survivor). Dry-run must be read-only; observability of the intended mutation must come from preview output only.

expedition.name: Harden draft lifecycle integrity
expedition.goal: Prove that draft creation/deletion is atomic, chain-safe, and approved without manual file surgery: (1) never manually rm/edit .synth/data/drafts/ files; all removal via CLI. (2) 'expedition delete' cleans up draft json+integrity files in the same transaction as the state mutation. (3) Fix --dry-run create bug that leaked draft file writes to disk. (4) Approved drafts are committed to the execution gate immediately rather than left as loose drafts.

expedition.name: Resolve ExecutionGate legacy-only branch enforcement
expedition.goal: Prove that execution branch enforcement accepts every canonical branch form the CLI generates: the EXECUTION_BRANCH_CHECK phase computes candidates without mission/expedition names and demands only the legacy raw-ID form (expedition/<missionId>/<expeditionId>), while ensureExpeditionBranch and assertExecutionBranch accept the preferred slug form — so starting any expedition on its slug-form branch is rejected by the gate that the CLI itself satisfied. Enrich the gate check with names from canonical state so both layers resolve identical candidate sets; cover with tests/execution-branch-gate.test.js

expedition.name: Debranch expedition completion
expedition.goal: Prove that concluding an expedition never requires its canonical branch to exist: CompleteExpedition leaves the branch-gated set (only StartExpedition remains gated, since its branch exists by construction at start time) because a completion-time branch may already be merged and deleted, may never have existed, or may be unavailable on another checkout. Align the CLI guard, ExecutionGate phase, and checkpoint step; update tests/execution-branch-gate.test.js

expedition.name: Unify expedition and mission termination commands
expedition.goal: DELIVERY ITEM: a concise termination model for expeditions and missions — clear, simple, leaving no room for pollution artifacts. Today the conclusion surface is scattered across complete, finish, archive, cancel (and archive doubles as cleanup fallback), each with different gates, evidence rules, and artifact side-effects; users cannot predict which command leaves which state behind. Collapse the surface into a minimal explicit model: few conclusion verbs with deterministic preconditions, exactly one event trail per termination path, and mandatory retirement of derived artifacts (drafts, loose files) in the same transition so terminal states never leave pollution behind

expedition.name: Investigate cross-branch event-log linearity during expedition closure
expedition.goal: Formalize the fast-forward-before-finish closure pattern proven live on d8a555db237507e5 and 20d934325ee30c1a: finishing on a canonical branch whose tip is a strict ancestor of main kept the derived event log linear across three branches and avoided replay divergence on later merges. Investigate (1) when lifecycle-event-bearing branches diverge from main and what replay and merge hazards follow, including interaction with existing repair tooling, (2) whether fast-forward reconciliation is always safe and how to detect mechanically when it is not, (3) what the CLI owes operators here: pre-finish ancestry verification, warnings, or automatic reconciliation. Deliverable: evidence-based findings plus zero or more follow-up expedition proposals for automation or documentation

expedition.name: Verify event-log lineage before lifecycle mutations
expedition.goal: Guard every lifecycle mutation (expedition approve, commit, start, finish, complete, archive, cancel) against forking the derived event log across branches: before mutating, compare the current branch's .synth/data/event-log.jsonl against the richest known log among local refs and origin/main; accept when it is a strict prefix (stale-but-safe, matching the proven fast-forward-before-finish protocol from investigation 3c84f699a7c932fc), block or warn when other refs carry exclusive events the current log lacks, and print reconciliation guidance (fast-forward when ancestor, explicit merge order otherwise). Implement in the CLI pre-flight layer, not inside the ExecutionGate, which stays untouched

expedition.name: Introduce DRY and SDK compliance certification into the expedition lifecycle
expedition.goal: Add a compliance check to the expedition lifecycle that statically inspects an expedition's deliverables for DRY violations and SDK-state-mutation misuse, and emits a machine-readable certification attached as expedition evidence. The certification is either CERTIFIED (full DRY + SDK evidence) or NOT_REQ (explicit, valid reasons the checks do not apply, e.g. no source deliverables or only derived/doc files). The check must run non-mutating: it adds NO extra lifecycle events beyond the evidence attachment.

expedition.name: Audit CLI command surface and decouple synth.js
expedition.goal: INVESTIGATION. Survey every CLI verb/subcommand (mission, expedition, evidence, validate, explain, docs, bootstrap, etc.) and quantify redundancy: overlapping procedures that can collapse into a smaller, memorable command set, reducing the operator 'knowledge quorum'. Map findings against existing related expeditions so the audit extends rather than duplicates them: bc9c51e0 (termination-model unification), dac069e8 (lifecycle simplification), ceaa59bf (bootstrap-performance). Identify where synth.js loads the full machinery (13-step bootstrap, all adapters, Mission Studio, Planning Cognition) on every invocation, and propose decoupling: lazy/deferred per-command loading, command-group entry points, and a thinner default path. Deliverable: a written audit plus follow-up expedition drafts minted from concrete findings (e.g. verb consolidation, lazy CLI loader).

expedition.name: Decouple synth.js: lazy-load command groups and thin CLI entrypoint
expedition.goal: Refactor src/cli/synth.ts so the top-level entrypoint performs only argument parsing + dispatch. Each command group (expedition, mission, program, explain, verify, docs, etc.) is loaded lazily on first invocation; the 13-step bootstrap, all adapters, Mission Studio, and Planning Cognition are imported only by commands that need them. Measurable target: cold-start of 'synth version' / 'synth status' must not load adapters or Mission Studio. Deliverable: lazy loader + per-group entrypoints + a cold-start benchmark.

expedition.name: Consolidate CLI verbs into a minimal, memorable command set
expedition.goal: Propose and implement a reduced command vocabulary that collapses redundant verbs while preserving capability. Coordinate with bc9c51e0 (termination unification): adopt a single lifecycle create->approve->start->finish with --disposition for expedition/mission; unify validate/verify/govern into 'check' (--dry-run|--full, --repair); unify status/checkpoint/explain status/report into 'status'; unify init/bootstrap/genesis/discover/migrate into 'init'. Deliverable: command-map migration plan + deprecated-alias shims + docs update.

expedition.name: CLI Lazy-Load Strategy
expedition.goal: Map the current synth.js bootstrap cost, identify command-group lazy boundaries, design the per-command-group lazy-loading model (shared bootstrap vs deferred domain graph), and define benchmarks and acceptance criteria so light commands stay bootstrap-free and heavy commands load only their group.

expedition.name: Migrate synth.js to Lazy-Load Model
expedition.goal: Migrate the monolithic synth.js heavy-load path to the per-command-group lazy-loading model defined by the CLI Lazy-Load Strategy expedition, preserving byte-identical command output and keeping light commands (version, help, status, explain replay/identity/resume/governance) bootstrap-free.

expedition.name: Audit expedition model: dependsOn enforcement and keep/remove decision
expedition.goal: Determine whether the expedition model enforces the dependsOn property. Current evidence: checkUpstreamDependencies (lifecycle-completion based) is advisory-only (reported as a warning in expedition check/doctor), while isBlockedByUpstreamGate (review-gate based) blocks execution in domain/execution.ts and governance/intake.ts. Decide which dependency mechanisms to keep, harden (e.g., enforce lifecycle completion at start), or remove, and recommend the target model.

expedition.name: Canonicalize and standardize logs
expedition.goal: Establish one canonical logging model for SYNTH: consolidate CLI error logs (cli-errors.jsonl), runtime diagnostics, event logs, and proof/temp artifacts into a single location, consistent schema, and rotation policy. Eliminate ad-hoc/duplicate logs (e.g., cli-errors.jsonl vs a referenced cli-errors.log, per-test temp logs under /var/folders) and standardize structured stdout vs diagnostic streams so operators and tooling depend on one shape.

expedition.name: Event schema versioning and migration registry
expedition.goal: Add schemaVersion to every event and a MigrationRegistry so replay survives event-shape evolution; version canonical-state by schema.

expedition.name: Fold legacy CLI verbs into the canonical command set
expedition.goal: Consolidate redundant verbs via deprecated-alias shims and a unified 'init' entrypoint, preserving first-contact/genesis/bootstrap/discover/governance subsystems and their tests. Canonical targets: status (was report/explain status), validate verify (was verify), docs agents (was project AGENTS.md), init --brownfield/--analyze/--greenfield (was bootstrap/discover/first-contact/genesis). Deprecate intent + migrate as load-bearing-for-alignment legacy verbs.

expedition.name: Allow archiving completed expeditions
expedition.goal: The 'expedition archive' lifecycle rule is inverted: it rejects archiving a COMPLETED expedition ('Only active or paused expeditions can be archived') while archiving is conceptually for finished/superseded work. Fix so a completed expedition can be archived (e.g., to retire a superseded duplicate). Scope: (1) intake.ts expedition.archive gate — add 'completed' to allowed source statuses (keep 'cancelled'/'archived' terminal, keep 'active'/'paused' allowed); (2) domain/planning.ts archiveExpedition — remove the 'cannot archive a completed expedition' invariant; (3) update the lifecycle comment at intake.ts:10-11; (4) add a regression test. Consider whether a dedicated 'superseded' disposition is cleaner than completed->archived and recommend in the plan.

expedition.name: Pointer-based evidence and derived-artifact exclusion from completion gate
expedition.goal: Reduce SYNTH's content redundancy and the commit-then-complete friction by (1) making evidence pointer-based: event-log/evidence records reference external artifacts by git SHA / content hash / URL instead of embedding content copies or full git diffs; completion records 'gitHead' as the realized-state pointer; (2) excluding derived/generated paths (proof/, dist/, *.integrity.json, canonical-state.json) from the DirtyWorkingTreeBlocksCompletion gate so only uncommitted IN-SCOPE SOURCE blocks completion; (3) keeping the event log as the authoritative provenance ledger while git remains the content store. Scope: locate the completion dirty-tree enforcement (cmdExpeditionComplete / CompleteExpedition capability) and the evidence-attach path; add a derived-path allowlist; record gitHead on EXPEDITION_COMPLETED. Preserve replay independence by keeping event-log.jsonl as the durable core. Add tests. Consider a short ADR noting the provenance-vs-content split.

expedition.name: Stage 0: Audit governance-cluster verbs & blast radius
expedition.goal: Map governance-cluster verbs (validate, verify, govern, checkpoint, approval, certify): every CLI invocation site, CI/script references (npm run govern), documentation mentions, and operator muscle-memory dependencies. Produce a blast-radius report identifying which renames break CI vs which are safe. Read-only research; no source changes.

expedition.name: Stage 1: Design target governance verb model (ADR)
expedition.goal: Decide the governance-cluster end-state: minimal (keep govern/validate/approval/certify; fold verify->validate verify + checkpoint->status) vs alias (add check deprecated shim for govern) vs full rename (govern->check). Produce an ADR with chosen model, rationale, and affected command/CI/doc graph. No source changes.

expedition.name: Stage 2: Implement safe governance folds (verify->validate verify, checkpoint->status)
expedition.goal: Low-risk deprecated-alias shims: verify->validate verify, checkpoint->status (pre-flight as a status mode). Add emitDeprecation notices, command-safety classification, help text. Keep govern/validate/approval/certify canonical. Build + verify.

expedition.name: Stage 3: Migrate CI/docs/scripts for any govern rename (gated, optional)
expedition.goal: ONLY if Stage 1 selects rename. Update npm run govern scripts, CI workflows, docs, operator refs from govern/validate to new verb. High blast radius; isolate from safe folds; requires Stage 1 sign-off. Build + full govern pipeline.

expedition.name: Stage 4: Verify govern-evolution (full pipeline + replay)
expedition.goal: After governance-cluster changes, run full govern pipeline and confirm replay consistency (synth explain replay) with no CI regression and operator flows intact.

expedition.name: Fix mission.approve gate scoping (checks active mission instead of target mission)
expedition.goal: intake.ts mission.approve resolves missionId = action.missionId || activeMission?.id; CLI passes no missionId, so it inspects the ACTIVE mission's executing expeditions, wrongly blocking approval of an UNRELATED mission. Fix: resolve the target mission from the approved draft/snapshot and check THAT mission for executing expeditions, so a mission with no executing expeditions can be approved even when another mission has a live expedition. See attached finding.

expedition.name: Implement mission new / expedition new commands (replace over-complicated mission create)
expedition.goal: Replace the draft-proposal mission create flow with a single canonicalizing 'mission new' (and 'expedition new') command, per the verb-consolidation plan. The new command should canonicalize a draft mission (emit MISSION_CREATED draft) so expeditions can be planned immediately, subsuming the 'mission create canonicalize draft' structural fix. See attached evidence.

expedition.name: Fix derived-state auto-commit (EXP-AUTO-COMMIT-001) to skip gitignored paths
expedition.goal: autoCommitDerivedState (src/cli/synth.ts ~351) builds an explicit git add path list that includes .synth/data/drafts/ (gitignored), causing the whole git add to error and the derived-state commit to abort, leaving event-log.jsonl/canonical-state.json staged-but-uncommitted after lifecycle transitions. Fix: exclude gitignored/derived-excluded paths before git add (filter via git check-ignore, or use git add -A which skips ignored). See attached finding.

expedition.name: Make expedition charters the primary enforced dependency source
expedition.goal: Make docs/expeditions/<id>.md charter **Depends On:** / **Blocks:** the single source of truth for expedition dependencies, eliminating the need for a --depends-on flag. (1) Ensure target 4ab7e9d2 expeditions have charters (generate if missing). (2) Make isBlockedByUpstreamGate (intake.ts:233, execution.ts:325) charter-aware so declared dependencies block downstream CLI commands/intents. (3) Wire the linear sequence by editing each charter Depends On to reference the previous expedition. Lifecycle (change/remove/reparent/edit) is a charter edit only - no dual source, no flag soup.

expedition.name: Chunk event log and decouple monolithic canonical-state into per-entity derived files
expedition.goal: Resolve the monolithic-state problem at both layers. (1) EVENT LOG: implement the already-designed PartitionedEvent chunking (src/infra/event-store.ts append(partition,event)/readPartition/readSegment) into .synth/data/event-stream/<partition>/<segment>.jsonl with an offset-ordered manifest, preserving deterministic replay. (2) PROJECTION: change StateStore.save (src/infra/state-store.ts:66) to write per-entity derived files (.synth/data/expeditions/<id>.json, .synth/data/missions/<id>.json) instead of one canonical-state.json; canonical-state.json becomes a generated aggregate (amend contract tracking rule). (3) dependsOn: make it a settable canonical attribute via expedition refine --depends-on (writes event, materialized into per-entity file). (4) Archive: relocate per-entity file to .synth/data/expeditions/archived/<id>.json (status marker), not a monolith shuffle. Single source of truth (event log) preserved; merge/review/scale improved.

expedition.name: Land validated code-fix batch: brownfield opacity, explain exit-code, quiet CI
expedition.goal: Merge the code changes validated on debug PR #331 (brownfield proof-opacity/bypass hardening, synth explain unknown-subcommand exit-code fix, CI log-noise reduction via SYNTH_QUIET_LOGS + dot reporter) into main under a single executing expedition via PR.

expedition.name: Chunk event log and decouple monolithic canonical-state into per-entity derived files
expedition.goal: Land the partitioned event-store + per-entity derived-state feature from expedition 01604a3df9d2785d: (1) PartitionedEvent chunking in src/infra/event-store.ts (.synth/data/event-stream/<partition>/<segment>.jsonl with offset-ordered manifest, deterministic replay preserved); (2) StateStore.save writes per-entity derived files instead of monolithic canonical-state.json (aggregate becomes generated); (3) dependsOn as settable canonical attribute via expedition refine --depends-on; (4) archive relocates per-entity file. Single source of truth (event log) preserved.

expedition.name: Resolve pre-existing test:all failures blocking green CI
expedition.goal: Investigate and plan resolution for the wired (test:all) test failures unrelated to monolith removal: decision-events, expedition-auto-commit, first-contact-project, first-contact-projection, installer-contract, installer-environment, installer-manifest, migration, package-distribution, synth-cli. Inventory the 39 non-wired (orphaned) failing tests. Deliverable: root-cause analysis + per-failure remediation plan.

expedition.name: Reduce test code duplication (DRY) in tests/
expedition.goal: Reduce test code duplication in tests/ using evidence .jscpd/tests/html/jscpd-report.json (273 clones, 5,629 duplicated lines). Discard duplicated boilerplate that does not belong (e.g. per-file test-runner loops), extract reusable fixtures/helpers, drive tests through the SDK, mock where needed, to lower DRY blocks. Scope: tests/ only. Deliverable: shared fixtures/helpers layer + migrated tests with materially lower jscpd duplication. src/ and scripts/ deferred to follow-up expeditions.

expedition.name: Reduce code duplication (DRY) in src/
expedition.goal: Follow-up to the tests dedupe expedition. Reduce code duplication in src/ using .jscpd/tests/html/jscpd-report.json plus a fresh src scan. Extract shared modules/helpers, consolidate repeated patterns, mock where sensible. Deliverable: consolidated src modules with materially lower jscpd duplication.

expedition.name: Reduce code duplication (DRY) in scripts/
expedition.goal: Follow-up to the tests dedupe expedition. Reduce code duplication in scripts/ using .jscpd/tests/html/jscpd-report.json plus a fresh scripts scan. Extract shared build/verify helpers, consolidate repeated logic. Deliverable: consolidated scripts with materially lower jscpd duplication.

expedition.name: Fix adversarial audit for partitioned event-stream
expedition.goal: Rewrite the P4 adversarial audit tamper/forgery/reorder attacks against the partitioned event-stream layout so tampering is actually exercised and detected; make govern proof pass

expedition.name: Derived-state staging correctness (auto-commit + ignore filtering)
expedition.goal: Fix auto-commit staging so lifecycle transitions always commit durable state and never fail on gitignored paths: call git check-ignore with --no-index so tracked-but-ignored paths are filtered correctly, stage only existing/changed durable artifacts instead of walking all of .synth/data, fall back to per-file adds so one bad path cannot kill the commit, and surface the autoCommit result (committed/commitHash/files/reason) in command JSON. Absorbs draft e8ba8f92 and the index-surgery half of the Reads-Never-Write plan (W2).

expedition.name: No write-on-read: content-keyed cache and pure status
expedition.goal: Make read-only commands read-only: key the charter dependency cache on content hashes instead of mtimes and relocate it to .synth/cache/ (untracked), make synth status compute AI metadata without persisting it while synth ai refresh remains the explicit regenerator, and extend the derived classification to .synth/ai/, .synth/cache/ and cli-errors.jsonl. Deliverable: status, doctor and capabilities leave a pristine tree clean.

expedition.name: Artifact policy and no-write-on-read regression guard
expedition.goal: Introduce src/state/artifact-policy.ts as the single classification of durable, input, derived, cache and legacy artifacts; make .gitignore, the auto-commit file list and the completion gate derive from it; add scripts/check-artifact-policy.js as a CI guard; add tests/no-write-on-read.test.js and tests/derived-state-commit.test.js so the invariants reads-never-write and derived-state-never-blocks-work are enforced by tests. Removes the stale tracked event-log.jsonl from the commit list and patterns.

expedition.name: Derived-state staging correctness (auto-commit + ignore filtering)
expedition.goal: Fix auto-commit staging so lifecycle transitions always commit durable state and never fail on gitignored paths: call git check-ignore with --no-index so tracked-but-ignored paths are filtered correctly, stage only existing/changed durable artifacts instead of walking all of .synth/data, fall back to per-file adds so one bad path cannot kill the commit, and surface the autoCommit result (committed/commitHash/files/reason) in command JSON. Absorbs draft e8ba8f92 and the index-surgery half of the Reads-Never-Write plan (W2).

expedition.name: Declared execution branches (--branch / --no-create)
expedition.goal: Implement ADR-056: accept --branch <name> on mission approve, expedition commit and expedition start; record the binding in the entity record and as a ledger event (MISSION_BRANCH_BOUND / EXPEDITION_BRANCH_BOUND payload {entityId, branch, declared, created, baseCommit, declaredBy}); resolve execution branches binding-first (binding -> taxonomy candidates -> trunk); validate declared names (git check-ref-format, local or origin), refuse a branch bound to another live entity (DECLARED_BRANCH_IN_USE) and a missing branch with --no-create (DECLARED_BRANCH_MISSING); emit the recorded BRANCH_POLICY_OVERRIDDEN warning for non-canonical declarations; add the config-level declaredPatterns (warning-softening only).

expedition.name: Ledger writer and delivery MVP (ADR-055 P1/P2)
expedition.goal: Implement ADR-055 phases P1-P2: anchor the ceremony ledger in a sparse, gitignored detached worktree (.synth/anchor) advanced by update-ref CAS with a lock and a dirty-ledger pre-check; route lifecycle ceremonies through the writer so each ceremony is one commit on the canonical branch; make doctor fail on uncommitted ledger, stale/missing anchor and ledger-ahead-of-main, with --fix performing worktree prune + re-add; add expedition deliver (push branch/publish PR, record EXPEDITION_DELIVERED) and expedition seal --merge-commit (verify the delivered tip is an ancestor of the merge commit, record EXPEDITION_INTEGRATED), plus the abandonment handoff block and deliveryPending marker.

expedition.name: Revisit testing and reporting infrastructure
expedition.goal: Re-examine the test chain (test:all, 111 npm-run steps), the governance profiler, and the reporting/logging surfaces. Decide which suites stay, which merge, which are retired, and how results are reported, so failures name a check and environment-dependent behavior is explicit. Replace the ad hoc decisions made while taming the codebase with a reviewed plan.

expedition.name: Verification coverage truthfulness: F1, F7–F10, and F15
expedition.goal: Make govern execute the canonical test:all task chain or fail loudly; migrate snapshot verification and branch-gate test assertions from legacy event-log.jsonl to event-stream; make explicit decisions for stale task tests; make evidence manifests cumulative or document per-call semantics; repair expedition-auto-commit convergence; and preserve the approved artifact and runtime-state policy.

expedition.name: EXP-TEST-001 Normalize logging & failure envelope
expedition.goal: Make every check failure emit structured JSON {checkId, status, duration, module, determinism, environment, failure:{file,line,assertion}} and prefix logs with [checkId]; introduce SYNTH_LOG_LEVEL, respect SYNTH_TASK_VERBOSE/SYNTH_QUIET_LOGS, extend test:clean-machine-output and test:governance-quiet-output.

expedition.name: EXP-TEST-002 Merge suites 114→~70
expedition.goal: Implement decision matrix from docs/plans/testing-and-reporting-infrastructure-review.md: keep ledger 6 distinct, execution 5, installer 7, documentation 3, governance 4; merge mission-studio 8→3, discovery 8→2, adapter 16→4, environment 5→4; add registration guard that every test:* task is in test:all or marked standalone.

expedition.name: EXP-TEST-003 Parallelize independent checks
expedition.goal: Use ParallelRunner for deterministic checks with no dependencies after build; keep contextual/non-deterministic sequential; measure speedup for govern --full; ensure no flakiness; add retry for non-deterministic.

expedition.name: EXP-TEST-004 Environment explicit
expedition.goal: Add environment field to GovernanceCheck and GovernSummary, surface environment-capability-report guidance in failures, make t.skip emit structured reason {environment:{baseBranch:missing}} with nextStep 'git fetch origin main --unshallow', introduce SYNTH_ENV=ci|local|container.

expedition.name: Dull status inbox for deliver/seal
expedition.goal: Make synth status print exact copy-pasteable deliver --branch and seal --merge-commit commands, fixing NoExecutionBranch fallback, ledgerBranch missing fallback, and shallow-clone hint, so fresh Arena sessions can seal after pull without extra queries.

expedition.name: Adapter configuration consolidated: declared vs detected
expedition.goal: Adapter configuration has no home. It is spread across five places with no authority order and no schema. (a) .synth/config.yaml holds a single `git:` block, parsed ad hoc by three independent modules (ledger/branch.ts:74, adapter/git-snapshot.ts:338, repository/branch-policy.ts) with no type, no loader module and no validation, so an unknown or misspelled key is silently ignored. (b) `synth init` writes detection results into the generated manifest under `adapters: {selected, config, diagnostics}` (cli/synth.ts:3070-3090) - a regenerable document, and absent from this repository manifest altogether. (c) .synth/context.json persists a repository classification (`repositoryType: brownfield-polyglot`, confidence, derivedFrom) but no adapter configuration. (d) `synth adapter configure repository path=. remote=origin defaultBranch=main promotionMode=direct` (cli/adapter.ts:11,74-86) is accepted and then lost: GitRepositoryAdapter.configure (adapters/repository/git.ts:187-199) merges into in-memory state and never writes, so the verb has no durable effect across a process restart. (e) Forge credentials are split between env GITHUB_TOKEN and a config schema that declares `token` required (adapters/github/adapter.ts:72), which invites a personal access token into tracked YAML. The consequence is measured, not theoretical: detectRecommendedAdapters already computes defaultBranch and remote (cli/detect-adapters.ts:113-119) and both are dropped, so the same fact is hardcoded three separate times (ledger/delivery.ts:347 defaults baseBranches to ["origin/main","main"] and no caller ever passes the option; ledger/branch.ts:49 LEDGER_FALLBACK_BRANCH = "main"; cli/adapter.ts:81 defaultBranch || "main"). Outcome required: (1) a typed `adapters:` section in .synth/config.yaml - adapters.repository.{provider,remote,baseBranch,snapshots,hooks} and adapters.forge.{provider,owner,repo,baseUrl} - read through one new loader module with schema validation that warns on unknown keys. (2) Detected observations written to .synth/cache/adapters.json (gitignored, artifact class `cache` per state/artifact-policy.ts:58, same precedent as dependency-records.json), each carrying value, confidence and derivedFrom, and including a git BINARY probe so that "git is not installed" is distinguishable from "git is installed but this directory is not a repository". Today first-contact onboard:detect returns byte-identical output for both cases and advises `synth adapter init` even when git is absent, which is advice the operator cannot follow. (3) A documented and tested authority order: CLI flag, then config.yaml, then cached detection, then built-in default - where the built-in default is provider none declaring no capabilities, never origin/main. (4) The three hardcoded branch defaults deleted and fed from configuration through the baseBranches option ledger/delivery.ts:347 already accepts. (5) `synth adapter configure --approve` promotes a detection proposal into config.yaml, plan-then-approve in the same shape as first-contact onboard --approve; this single mechanism is what makes the greenfield offer ("git is installed, this is not a repository - initialise it?") and the brownfield offer ("a repository and a GitHub remote were detected - configure the forge adapter?") the same code path. (6) Credentials resolved from env or a secret store only, with `token` removed from the GitHub adapter required config schema. (7) The existing `git:` block migrated to adapters.repository.* with a deprecation warning on read, and `git.ledgerBranch` retired: the ledger branch is inferred from the checkout when it matches branchPolicy.declaredPatterns, with trunk as the last resort rather than the first. (8) The ledger-branch fallback order corrected - a stale configured value plus a stale .synth/data/ledger.json record (currently arena/c5db653e-synth) resolve to local `main` today, which would commit governance state onto the trunk branch instead of the declared operator checkout; a checkout matching a declared pattern must win over trunk. Acceptance: the three-system matrix (no git at all / git installed without a repository / git installed with a repository) yields distinct, truthful recognition output and identical ledger behaviour in all three; no repository or branch value is hardcoded outside the loader documented defaults; `synth adapter configure` survives a process restart; no secret can be written into .synth/config.yaml; and the ledger records ceremonies with zero VCS present, reporting verification as unavailable rather than failing.

expedition.name: Verification sees the whole event log
expedition.goal: The framework integrity evidence is vacuous on any repository whose event log has been chunked. src/verification/context.ts:44,62 computes `hasEventLog = migratedEvents.length > 0 || await pathExists(eventLogPath)` where eventLogPath is sdk.paths.eventLogFile(root) - the legacy single file .synth/data/event-log.jsonl. This repository log lives at .synth/data/event-stream/partition-<n>/segment-XXXX.jsonl (four partitions, 442 events), the layout documented at src/runtime/governance-resolver.ts:84 and read by SegmentStore (src/infra/event-store.ts:325). So hasEventLog is false, and in order: verification/checks.ts:44 returns ReplayIntegrity "pass" with the message "No event log present; replay integrity is vacuously satisfied"; checks.ts:117 and checks.ts:386 skip their event-log-gated assertions; verification/engine.ts:29 skips replay entirely; and cli/synth.ts:862-869 (verifyReplayHealth) reports "No event log present; replay skipped" inside `synth checkpoint`. At the same moment `synth explain replay` reads the partitioned store correctly and reports 442 events, consistent, chain valid. The two disagree and the disagreement is invisible: the check whose only job is proving the ledger is intact reports success without ever looking at it. Every green validate, govern and full-govern run on a chunked repository - including the one that certified PR #343 - carried that vacuous pass. The same legacy-path assumption is spread across at least seven further call sites: cli/bootstrap-apply.ts:235, cli/explain-observability.ts:110, cli/explain-paths.ts:57, cli/explain-replay-light.ts:49, cli/first-contact.ts:746, 780 and 826. Two complications make this more than a one-line fix. First, THREE layouts coexist in the codebase: the legacy single file, event-stream/partition-<n>.jsonl (still implemented by PartitionStore.filePath at event-store.ts:161-162) and the current event-stream/partition-<n>/segment-XXXX.jsonl - so the codebase carries two contradictory ideas of what a partition is. Second, the vocabulary cannot express the truth: verification/types.ts:14 declares `CheckStatus = "pass" | "fail" | "warn"` with no skipped value, which is precisely why an absent log is reported as a pass instead of as a non-result. Outcome required: (1) ONE authority for where the event log is and whether there is one - a single resolver recognising all three layouts and returning present, layout, paths and eventCount - consumed by verification/context, verifyReplayHealth and every call site listed above; after this, no module may construct or test the legacy path directly. (2) A vacuous pass becomes impossible: CheckStatus gains `skipped` carrying a structured reason (the same shape EXP-TEST-004 proposes for test skips), ReplayIntegrity reports skipped with reason no-event-log when there is genuinely no log, and reports the eventCount it actually replayed when there is one. (3) `synth checkpoint` replay step names the layout and the event count verified, and can never again print "No event log present" for a repository holding 442 events. (4) PartitionStore stale partition-<n>.jsonl naming is either reconciled with the segment layout or explicitly marked legacy-read-only, so two contradictory partition layouts stop shipping side by side. (5) Tests pin all three layouts: a segment-partitioned ledger must yield a ReplayIntegrity result naming its eventCount; a legacy single-file ledger must still verify; an empty project must report skipped rather than pass; and a regression guard must fail if any module reintroduces a direct legacy-path existence check. Acceptance: on this repository `synth checkpoint` and `synth validate` report replay over 442 events instead of skipping; ReplayIntegrity and `explain replay` agree; and no verification check is able to report pass without having read the log.
